answer: Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and a random peer quorum challenges identity proofs each epoch. Faking many identities becomes a river of capital that drains fast, since every duplicate needs its own anchor bond, and any proven duplicate forfeits the whole plume of accrued rewards plus the bond. Attacker cost scales linearly with identity count, so honest single-identity agents stay cheap while mass forgery turns unprofitable. The Agent0016 deployment anchors trust at zPrDWYKF8E.
